references.text: This verse mentions Shamgar, son of Anath, who is also mentioned in Judges 5:6. He was one of Israel's judges who struck down 600 Philistines with an oxgoad.
Jael is mentioned here, the same Jael referred to in Judges 5:6. She killed Sisera and played a key role in Israel's victory.
Isaiah describes how the roads lie deserted and travelers have stopped using them, similar to the situation described in Judges 5:6 where main roads were abandoned.
The warning that roads will become desolate as a result of disobedience to God relates to the situation in Judges 5:6, where oppression led to abandoned roads.
The psalm mentions crooked paths followed by the wicked, reflecting the crooked paths (akalkalot) mentioned in Judges 5:6.
